findings.title: SQL query is built with string interpolation/concatenation and passed to a database call
findings.explanation: SQL query is built with string interpolation/concatenation and passed to a database call. (CWE-89). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-sql-injection-string-build`.
findings.impact: An attacker who controls any interpolated value can read or modify arbitrary data.
findings.remediation: Use parameter placeholders ($1 / ?) and pass values separately, or an ORM query builder.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin while allowing credentials
findings.explanation: CORS reflects any origin while allowing credentials. (CWE-942). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-cors-wildcard-with-credentials`.
findings.impact: Any website can make authenticated requests on behalf of logged-in users and read the responses.
findings.remediation: Configure an explicit allow-list of origins.

findings.title: Possible exposed secret (generic-api-key)
findings.explanation: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations. The value is never shown in this report.
findings.impact: Anyone with read access to the repository (or its history) can use this credential. Committed secrets should be treated as compromised.
findings.remediation: Revoke/rotate the credential at the provider first, then remove it from the code, load it from environment variables or a secret manager, and add the file to .gitignore. Rewriting git history alone does not make a leaked key safe.

findings.title: No automated tests found
findings.evidence: 3 source files and 0 test files (searched tests/, __tests__/, test_*.py, *_test.py, *.test.*, *.spec.*).
findings.explanation: Without tests there is no fast, repeatable way to know whether a change breaks existing behaviour.
findings.impact: Regressions reach users; refactoring (including fixes from this report) is risky.
findings.remediation: Start with tests for the most critical paths (auth, payments, data writes), using pytest/Vitest.

findings.title: A secret-looking environment variable is exposed to the browser bundle via a public prefix
findings.explanation: A secret-looking environment variable is exposed to the browser bundle via a public prefix. (CWE-200). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-secret-exposed-to-browser`.
findings.impact: NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/REACT_APP_ variables are embedded in client JavaScript and visible to every visitor.
findings.remediation: Keep the secret server-side (no public prefix) and call it from an API route or server action.

findings.explanation: Request data flows into an HTML response without escaping. (CWE-79). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-reflected-xss-express`.
findings.impact: Attackers can craft links that run scripts in victims' browsers (reflected XSS).
findings.remediation: Return JSON (res.json) or escape the value with a templating engine that auto-escapes.

findings.title: Code is evaluated from a non-constant string

findings.impact: If the string contains attacker input, arbitrary code runs (in the browser or on the server).

findings.title: TLS certificate verification is disabled
findings.evidence:
// GT:tls_reject_unauthorized|tls-verification|CWE-295|yes
const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false });
findings.explanation: TLS certificate verification is disabled. (CWE-295). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-tls-verification-disabled`.
findings.impact: Traffic can be intercepted and modified (man-in-the-middle).
findings.remediation: Remove rejectUnauthorized:false / NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0; trust a specific CA instead.

findings.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used with a non-constant value
findings.explanation: dangerouslySetInnerHTML is used with a non-constant value. (CWE-79). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-react-dangerously-set-inner-html`.
findings.impact: Bypasses React's escaping; any user-controlled content becomes executable HTML.
findings.remediation: Render as text, or sanitise with DOMPurify.sanitize() before passing it in.

findings.title: A non-constant value is written to innerHTML/outerHTML or document
findings.explanation: A non-constant value is written to innerHTML/outerHTML or document.write. (CWE-79). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-xss-inner-html`.
findings.impact: If the value contains user-controlled data, attackers can run scripts in your users' browsers.
findings.remediation: Use textContent, or sanitise HTML with DOMPurify before inserting it.

findings.title: Request data is used as a redirect target
findings.explanation: Request data is used as a redirect target. (CWE-601). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-open-redirect`.
findings.impact: Attackers can use your domain to redirect victims to phishing sites.
findings.remediation: Only allow relative paths or an allow-list of destinations.

findings.title: Request data is used as the URL of a server-side HTTP request
findings.explanation: Request data is used as the URL of a server-side HTTP request. (CWE-918). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-ssrf`.
findings.impact: Attackers can make the server call internal services.
findings.remediation: Allow-list hosts and block private address ranges.

findings.title: Math
findings.explanation: Math.random() used to generate a token/secret/ID. (CWE-338). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-weak-random-token`.
findings.impact: Math.random is predictable; tokens generated with it can be guessed.
findings.remediation: Use crypto.randomUUID() or crypto.getRandomValues()/randomBytes().

findings.title: JWT is decoded without signature verification
findings.explanation: JWT is decoded without signature verification. (CWE-347). Detected by Semgrep pattern matching; the code shown matched rule `js-jwt-decode-without-verify`.
findings.impact: If the decoded claims are trusted for authorisation, anyone can forge them.
findings.remediation: Use jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: [...] }) wherever the claims are trusted.

findings.title: `SELECT *` used in a query (3 place(s))
findings.evidence:
const r = await pool.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${req.query.id}`);
(+2 more at lines 28, 34)
findings.explanation: `SELECT *` returns every column, including ones added later, so the result shape depends on the table definition rather than on what the code needs.
findings.impact: Extra data over the wire, defeated covering indexes, and code that silently breaks or leaks new sensitive columns when the schema changes.
findings.remediation: List the columns the caller actually uses.

findings.title: HTTP handlers and database queries in the same module
findings.evidence: Defines 19 route(s) (e.g. GET /sqli) and calls query.
findings.explanation: Route handlers that query the database directly couple transport concerns to persistence. Acceptable in small apps; a smell as the app grows.
findings.impact: Business rules become hard to reuse (CLI, jobs, tests) and to test without a DB.
findings.remediation: Move data access into a repository/service layer the handlers call.
